facts.ALB: A black double-headed eagle on red. Albanians call their country Shqipëria, often linked to 'land of eagles'.
facts.DZA: Green and white halves with a red crescent and star.
facts.AND: Blue-yellow-red with a coat of arms in the middle. Without the arms it would look just like Chad's or Romania's.
facts.AGO: Red over black with a yellow half cog-wheel and machete, inspired by the Soviet hammer and sickle.
facts.ARG: Light blue and white stripes with the golden 'Sun of May' in the middle.
facts.ARM: Red, blue and orange horizontal stripes.
facts.AUS: Union Jack in the corner, a big seven-pointed Commonwealth Star below it, and the Southern Cross. Australia's stars are white; New Zealand's are red.
facts.AUT: Red-white-red horizontal stripes, one of the oldest national flags in the world.
facts.AZE: Blue-red-green with a white crescent and an eight-pointed star.
facts.BHS: A black triangle with aquamarine and gold stripes: the sea and the sand.
facts.BHR: Red with a white serrated band of five points. Qatar's looks similar but is maroon with nine points.
facts.BGD: A red disc on green. The disc sits slightly towards the pole so it looks centred when the flag flies.
facts.BRB: Blue-gold-blue with a black trident head. The trident's shaft is broken, symbolising the break from colonial rule.
facts.BLR: Red and green with a red-and-white folk ornament along the hoist.
facts.BEL: Black-yellow-red VERTICAL stripes. Germany has the same colours, but horizontal.
facts.BLZ: Blue with red edges and a coat of arms showing two woodcutters. One of the few national flags with people on it.
facts.BTN: A white thunder dragon (Druk). Bhutan is called 'Land of the Thunder Dragon'.
facts.BIH: Blue with a yellow triangle and a line of white stars. The triangle roughly echoes the country's shape.
facts.BWA: Light blue with a black stripe edged in white.
facts.BRA: A blue globe on a yellow diamond on green. The stars show the night sky over Rio on 15 November 1889, one star per state. Motto: 'Ordem e Progresso'.
facts.KHM: Blue and red with Angkor Wat, the famous temple complex, in white.
facts.CMR: Green-red-yellow vertical stripes with a yellow star in the middle.
facts.CAN: The red maple leaf between two red bands, adopted in 1965.
facts.CPV: Blue with white and red stripes and a ring of ten stars, one per main island.
facts.TCD: Blue-yellow-red vertical stripes. Almost identical to Romania's; Chad's blue is slightly darker.
facts.CHL: White and red with a blue square and a white star. Looks a lot like the flag of Texas.
facts.CHN: Red with one large and four small yellow stars.
facts.COL: Yellow-blue-red, with the yellow band twice as wide as the others.
facts.COD: Sky blue with a red diagonal stripe edged in yellow, and a yellow star in the corner.
facts.CRI: Blue-white-red-white-blue stripes, with the red band double width.
facts.CIV: Orange-white-green vertical stripes. Ireland's flag is the mirror image: green-white-orange.
facts.HRV: Red-white-blue with a red-and-white checkerboard shield.
facts.CUB: Blue and white stripes with a red triangle and a white star. Puerto Rico's has the same design with the colours swapped.
facts.CYP: A copper-coloured map of the island on white. One of only two flags showing the country's map (Kosovo's is the other).
facts.CZE: White over red with a blue triangle from the left.
facts.DNK: The Dannebrog: said to be the oldest national flag still in use. The Nordic cross design started here.
facts.DOM: A white cross splitting blue and red squares. The coat of arms shows a Bible, the only national flag with one.
facts.ECU: Yellow-blue-red like Colombia, but with a coat of arms topped by a condor.
facts.EGY: Red-white-black with the golden Eagle of Saladin.
facts.SLV: Blue-white-blue with a coat of arms. Nicaragua's looks similar.
facts.SWZ: A Nguni shield and two spears on blue, yellow and red stripes.
facts.ETH: Green-yellow-red with a blue disc and star. Ethiopia's colours inspired many other African flags.
facts.FJI: Light blue with the Union Jack and a shield.
facts.FIN: A blue Nordic cross on white, often said to stand for lakes and snow.
facts.GMB: Red, blue and green stripes. The blue in the middle is the Gambia River, which runs through the whole country.
facts.GEO: The 'five cross flag': a big red cross and four small ones on white.
facts.DEU: Black-red-gold horizontal stripes. Belgium has the same colours, but vertical.
facts.GHA: Red-gold-green with a black star, a symbol of African freedom.
facts.GRC: Nine blue and white stripes, said to match the nine syllables of 'Eleftheria i Thanatos' (Freedom or Death).
facts.GTM: Sky blue-white-sky blue vertical stripes with a quetzal bird on the coat of arms.
facts.GIN: Red-yellow-green vertical stripes. Mali's flag is the mirror image.
facts.GUY: 'The Golden Arrowhead': a yellow arrow on green, with a red triangle.
facts.HTI: Blue over red with a coat of arms. Haiti and Liechtenstein only noticed their flags matched at the 1936 Olympics; Liechtenstein then added a crown.
facts.HND: Blue-white-blue with five blue stars, one for each member of the old Central American Federation.
facts.ISL: A red cross edged in white on blue. Norway's uses the same colours the other way round.
facts.IND: Saffron-white-green with the blue Ashoka Chakra, a wheel with 24 spokes.
facts.IDN: Red over white. Same as Monaco's, except Monaco's is squarer. Poland's is white over red.
facts.IRN: Green-white-red with a red emblem; 'Allahu Akbar' is written 22 times along the stripe edges.
facts.IRQ: Red-white-black with green Arabic script in the middle.
facts.IRL: Green-white-orange: green for the Gaelic tradition, orange for Protestants, and white for peace between them.
facts.ISR: A blue Star of David between two blue stripes, based on a Jewish prayer shawl.
facts.ITA: Green-white-red vertical stripes. Mexico's has the same colours with an eagle in the middle.
facts.JAM: A gold diagonal cross with green and black triangles. The only national flag with no red, white or blue.
facts.JPN: A red disc on white, called Hinomaru: 'circle of the sun'.
facts.JOR: Black-white-green with a red triangle holding a white seven-pointed star. Palestine's is the same without the star.
facts.KAZ: Sky blue with a golden sun, a soaring eagle and a pattern along the hoist.
facts.KEN: Black-red-green with white edges and a Maasai shield and spears.
facts.KIR: A frigatebird flying over a sun rising from the waves.
facts.XKX: A gold map of Kosovo on blue with six white stars. One of only two flags showing the country's map (Cyprus's is the other).
facts.KWT: Green-white-red with a black trapezoid on the left.
facts.KGZ: A yellow sun on red. Its 40 rays stand for 40 tribes; in the middle is the crown of a yurt.
facts.LAO: Red-blue-red with a white disc, often described as the moon over the Mekong.
facts.LVA: A dark carmine red with a thin white stripe. The colour is unique to Latvia.
facts.LBN: A green cedar tree between red stripes.
facts.LSO: Blue-white-green with a black Basotho hat.
facts.LBR: Red and white stripes with one white star on blue, modelled on the US flag.
facts.LBY: Red-black-green with a white crescent and star.
facts.LIE: Blue over red with a gold crown, added after the 1936 Olympics mix-up with Haiti.
facts.LUX: Red-white-light blue. Like the Netherlands, but with a lighter blue.
facts.MDG: A white vertical band with red and green horizontal stripes.
facts.MWI: Black-red-green with a red rising sun in the black band.
facts.MYS: 'Jalur Gemilang': 14 red and white stripes with a yellow crescent and a 14-pointed star.
facts.MDV: A green rectangle with a white crescent on red.
facts.MLI: Green-yellow-red vertical stripes. Guinea's is the mirror image; Senegal's adds a star.
facts.MLT: White and red with the George Cross in the corner, awarded for courage during World War II.
facts.MRT: Green with a gold crescent and star; red stripes were added top and bottom in 2017.
facts.MUS: Four horizontal stripes: red, blue, yellow, green.
facts.MEX: Green-white-red with an eagle on a cactus eating a snake, the founding legend of Tenochtitlan (today's Mexico City).
facts.MDA: Blue-yellow-red with an eagle coat of arms. Close to Romania's and Chad's.
facts.MCO: Red over white, just like Indonesia but squarer.
facts.MNG: Red-blue-red with the golden Soyombo symbol.
facts.MNE: Red with a gold border and a gold double-headed eagle.
facts.MAR: A green five-pointed star outlined on red.
facts.MOZ: The only national flag with a modern rifle: an AK-47 crossed with a hoe, on top of a book.
facts.MMR: Yellow-green-red with a large white star.
facts.NAM: A diagonal red band edged in white between blue and green, with a golden sun.
facts.NPL: The only national flag that isn't a rectangle: two stacked pennants.
facts.NLD: Red-white-blue horizontal stripes. It was originally orange-white-blue, after William of Orange.
facts.NZL: Union Jack with four red stars edged in white (the Southern Cross). Australia's stars are white and there are more of them.
facts.NIC: Blue-white-blue with a triangle showing five volcanoes and a rainbow.
facts.NER: Orange-white-green with an orange circle. Looks like India's without the wheel.
facts.PRK: Blue-red-blue with a red star on a white disc.
facts.MKD: A yellow sun on red, with eight rays spreading to the edges.
facts.NOR: A blue cross edged in white on red. Iceland uses the same colours the other way round.
facts.PAK: Dark green with a white crescent and star, and a white stripe for religious minorities.
facts.PLW: A yellow disc (the moon) on light blue.
facts.PSE: Black-white-green with a red triangle. Jordan's is the same plus a white star.
facts.PAN: Four quarters: two white with a blue and a red star, one red, one blue.
facts.PNG: Split diagonally red and black, with a bird of paradise and the Southern Cross.
facts.PRY: Red-white-blue. The only national flag with a different emblem on the front and the back.
facts.PHL: Blue over red with a white triangle and a sun. In wartime it's flown upside down, red on top.
facts.POL: White over red. Indonesia and Monaco are the upside-down version.
facts.PRT: Green and red with a coat of arms on an armillary sphere, an old navigation instrument.
facts.QAT: Maroon with a white serrated band of nine points. Bahrain's is red with five points.
facts.ROU: Blue-yellow-red vertical stripes. Almost identical to Chad's.
facts.RWA: Blue-yellow-green with a yellow sun in the corner.
facts.SAU: Green with the Islamic creed in white Arabic script and a sword. Because of the creed it's never flown at half-mast.
facts.SEN: Green-yellow-red with a green star in the middle. Mali's plus a star.
facts.SRB: Red-blue-white with a coat of arms: Russia's colours upside down.
facts.SYC: Five coloured bands fanning out from the bottom-left corner.
facts.SGP: Red over white with a crescent moon and five stars.
facts.SVK: White-blue-red with a shield showing a white double cross on three blue hills.
facts.SVN: White-blue-red with a shield showing Mount Triglav. Like Slovakia's, but the shield sits higher in the corner.
facts.SOM: A white star on light blue. Its five points stand for five regions where Somalis live.
facts.ZAF: A sideways Y in six colours, adopted in 1994 when apartheid ended: different paths coming together.
facts.KOR: 'Taegukgi': a red and blue yin-yang with four black trigrams on white.
facts.ESP: Red-yellow-red, with the yellow twice as wide and the coat of arms off-centre.
facts.LKA: A golden lion holding a sword, with green and orange stripes for the Muslim and Tamil minorities.
facts.SWE: A yellow Nordic cross on blue.
facts.CHE: A white cross on red. One of only two square national flags (Vatican City's is the other).
facts.TWN: Red with a blue corner holding a white sun: 'Blue Sky, White Sun, and a Wholly Red Earth'.
facts.TZA: A black diagonal band edged in yellow between green and blue triangles.
facts.THA: Red-white-blue-white-red, with the blue band in the middle twice as wide.
facts.TTO: Red with a black diagonal band edged in white.
facts.TUN: Red with a white disc holding a red crescent and star. Turkey's has no disc.
facts.TUR: A white crescent and star on red.
facts.TKM: Green with a vertical stripe of five carpet patterns (guls), one for each major tribe.
facts.UGA: Black-yellow-red stripes with a grey crowned crane in a white circle.
facts.UKR: Blue over yellow, often described as blue sky over wheat fields.
facts.ARE: A red vertical bar with green-white-black horizontal stripes.
facts.GBR: The Union Jack: the crosses of St George (England), St Andrew (Scotland) and St Patrick (Ireland). Wales isn't included.
facts.USA: 50 stars for the states and 13 stripes for the original colonies.
facts.URY: Nine white and blue stripes with the Sun of May in the corner, the same sun as Argentina's.
facts.UZB: Blue-white-green with a crescent and 12 stars.
facts.VAT: Square, yellow and white, with the crossed keys of Saint Peter.
facts.VEN: Yellow-blue-red with an arc of eight white stars.
facts.VNM: A yellow five-pointed star on red.
facts.YEM: Plain red-white-black, like Egypt's and Iraq's without an emblem.
facts.ZMB: Green with an orange eagle above red, black and orange bars.
facts.ZWE: Green, yellow, red and black stripes with the Zimbabwe Bird, a carving from Great Zimbabwe.
facts.GRL: Split white and red with a circle in the opposite colours: the sun sinking below the ice.
facts.FRO: A red cross edged in blue on white.
facts.ALA: A red cross edged in yellow on blue: Sweden's colours plus a red cross.
facts.HKG: A white bauhinia flower on red.
facts.PRI: Red and white stripes with a blue triangle and a white star. Cuba's flag with the colours swapped.

lookalikes.tip: Blue-yellow-red vertical stripes: Chad and Romania are plain (Chad's blue is darker). Andorra and Moldova have a coat of arms in the middle, and Moldova's is an eagle.
Red over white is Indonesia (long) or Monaco (squarer). White over red is Poland. Red over white with a moon and stars is Singapore.
Green-white-orange is Ireland; orange-white-green is Ivory Coast. Green-white-red is Italy, plus an eagle for Mexico.
The Netherlands has a dark blue bottom stripe; Luxembourg's is light blue.
White-blue-red: Russia is plain; Slovakia and Slovenia add a shield (Slovakia's double cross is bigger and lower). Serbia is red-blue-white.

Nordic crosses: Denmark is white on red; Norway is blue on red; Iceland is red on blue; Sweden is yellow on blue; Finland is blue on white; the Faroes are red on white; Åland is red and yellow on blue.
Australia has white stars and a big seven-pointed star under the Union Jack. New Zealand has four red stars.
Green-yellow-red: Mali is plain, Senegal adds a green star, Cameroon a yellow one. Guinea is the reverse, red-yellow-green.
Yellow-blue-red: Colombia is plain with a wide yellow band; Ecuador adds a coat of arms with a condor; Venezuela has equal stripes and an arc of stars.
Blue over red: Liechtenstein has a gold crown in the corner, Haiti a coat of arms in the middle.
Qatar is maroon with nine points; Bahrain is bright red with five.
Cuba has blue stripes and a red triangle; Puerto Rico has red stripes and a blue triangle.
Pan-Arab colours: Palestine has a red triangle, Jordan the same plus a star, Sudan a green triangle, Kuwait a black trapezoid, and the UAE a red vertical bar.
Red-white-black: Yemen is plain, Egypt has a golden eagle, and Iraq has green writing.

Central American blue and white: Honduras has five blue stars; Nicaragua's emblem has volcanoes and a rainbow; El Salvador's has flags and a laurel wreath. Guatemala's stripes are vertical, with a quetzal bird.
Argentina has three stripes with the sun in the middle; Uruguay has nine stripes with the sun in the corner.
Same colours: Belgium's stripes are vertical, Germany's horizontal.
Tunisia's crescent and star sit inside a white disc; Turkey's don't.
A red disc on white is Japan; on green, Bangladesh. A yellow disc on blue is Palau.
India has a blue wheel; Niger has a plain orange circle and is squarer.
Stripes with a blue corner: the USA has 50 stars, Liberia one star, and Malaysia a crescent and a star.
Red-white-red: horizontal is Austria (Latvia is darker with a thin white stripe; Lebanon has a cedar). Vertical is Peru, or Canada with its maple leaf.
Yellow on red: Vietnam has one big star in the middle; China has five stars in the corner.
